chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Wasil from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Hospitality is for the first day, and the second, and the third, and whatever is after that, so it is a charity by which you give charity upon him.'

He said: Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you lodge upon his brother until he burdens him with it.' It was said, 'O Rasool-Allah, how does he burden him?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Until there is not in his possession anything that he can spend upon him.'

key_terms.يُوثِمَهُ: To burden / To impose a cost upon

ai.seo_question: What is the duration of obligatory hospitality in Islam and how is it distinguished from charity?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the Sunnah of hospitality, distinguishing the obligatory three-day period from the voluntary charity extended thereafter, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. The second part clarifies the principle of 'not burdening' (la yukallif), ensuring the guest's stay does not cause financial hardship, thereby preserving the dignity of the host-guest relationship.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Wasil, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The hospitality is on the first day, and the second, and the third, and whatever is after that, so it is a charity, you have given charity with it upon him’.

He (the narrator) said: ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not one of you should lodge upon his brother until he is difficult with him’. It was said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! How is he difficult upon him?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Until there does not happen to be anything in his presence what he can spend upon him’.
en.sarwar: 2. AI-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad, from Wasil, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Special treatment for a guest is in the first day, in the second day and on the third day. Anything beyond this is charity that you give to him.’
He (the Messenger of Allah) then said, ‘One of you must not stay with his brother (in belief) to cause him difficulties.’ It was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can he cause difficulties?’
He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘He stays with him until he (the host) has nothing else to spend for him.’”
